name: hydra-image-processor
raw_meta_yaml:
context:
  version: "4.0.0"

package:
  name: "hydra-image-processor"
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/ericwait/hydra-image-processor/archive/refs/tags/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: a3e2dd438e9c825d37491ecd2da048dddfe0222bd49f71138fff8a29ed263b15

build:
  skip:
    - osx
    - match(cuda_compiler_version, "==None")
  # scikit-build-core drives CMake, compiles the CUDA extension, and installs
  # the package. conda-forge's compiler activation exports CMAKE_ARGS, which
  # scikit-build-core forwards to CMake, so NO source patches are required.
  script:
    env:
      # Without this CMake picks the Visual Studio generator on Windows,
      # which needs the CUDA VS-integration files that the conda-forge nvcc
      # package does not ship. Ninja drives nvcc directly on all platforms.
      CMAKE_GENERATOR: Ninja
    content:
      # The vs2022 activation exports CMAKE_GENERATOR_PLATFORM/TOOLSET for
      # the Visual Studio generator when they are unset; Ninja rejects
      # platform specifications, so clear them after activation.
      - if: win
        then:
          - set CMAKE_GENERATOR_PLATFORM=
          - set CMAKE_GENERATOR_TOOLSET=
      - ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
  string: cuda${{ cuda_compiler_version | version_to_buildstring }}_np${{ numpy | version_to_buildstring }}_py${{ python | version_to_buildstring }}_h${{ hash }}_${{ build_number }}
  number: 2

# c.f. https://github.com/conda-forge/cuda-feedstock/blob/main/recipe/doc/recipe_guide.md
requirements:
  build:
    - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
    - ${{ compiler("cxx") }}
    - ${{ compiler("cuda") }}
    - if: linux and aarch64
      then: arm-variant * ${{ arm_variant_type }}
    - cmake
    - ninja
    - if: build_platform != host_platform
      then:
        - cross-python_${{ host_platform }}
        - python
        - numpy
  host:
    - cuda-version ${{ cuda_compiler_version }}.*
    - python
    - pip
    - scikit-build-core
    - numpy
    - if: linux
      then: libgomp
      else: llvm-openmp
  run:
    - ${{ pin_compatible("cuda-version", lower_bound="x", upper_bound="x") }}
    - python
    - numpy

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - hydra_image_processor
        - HIP
        - Hydra

about:
  summary: "GPU accelerated image processing library"
  description: |
    Hydra Image Processor is a hardware accelerated signal processing library
    written with CUDA. HIP aims to create a signal processing library that can
    be incorporated into many software tools.
  license: BSD-3-Clause
  license_file: license.txt
  homepage: https://hydraimageprocessor.com/
  repository: https://github.com/ericwait/hydra-image-processor
  documentation: https://hydraimageprocessor.com/

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - ericwait
    - matthewfeickert
